channel.title: Gaming on Best of AI
channel.description: Recent content in Gaming on Best of AI

item.title: Leetify
item.description:
Leetify is an analytics and coaching tool for Counter-Strike players. After a match, it reads the demo data and produces a report with ratings across aim, positioning, and use of grenades, plus round-by-round breakdowns that show why a round was won or lost. Players compare themselves with others at their level.

Team features support scrims and coaching. Coaches review stats across players, see where the team struggles, and track improvement over time. A public profile shows a player’s progress, and a leaderboard ranks users, with an optional paid tier for deeper analysis.

item.title: Mobalytics
item.description:
Mobalytics is a gaming analytics and coaching site. Players link their accounts, and the tool analyzes their games, scoring performance across areas like farming, vision, and teamfights. A profile shows trends over time and compares the player with others at their rank.

Coaching features set it apart. The platform highlights patterns in mistakes and suggests focus areas, offers guides for champions and builds, and provides an overlay with in-game tips. Premium plans add deeper analysis and AI-generated feedback.

item.title: AI Dungeon
item.description:
AI Dungeon pioneered AI storytelling games. You choose a setting, such as fantasy, mystery, or survival, or create your own, and then type what your character does. The AI responds with what happens next, with no fixed script, so you can attempt anything and the story adapts. The result is a different kind of game from traditional adventures, with open-ended possibilities and sometimes surprising turns.

Creative tools are part of the platform. Players can build custom scenarios with their own characters and rules, share them with the community, and play adventures others have made. Story features let you edit and redo the AI’s output to steer the narrative, and memory settings help it keep track of characters and plot. Multiplayer modes let friends play together in one story.

item.title: Charisma.ai
item.description:
Charisma.ai helps creators combine writing with generative AI. Instead of leaving a character entirely to a language model, creators design a story with scenes, goals, and character personalities, and the platform lets characters respond flexibly to what players say while steering the conversation along the intended narrative. This approach aims to keep stories coherent and on message, which is a common problem with free-form AI dialogue.

Tools include a visual story editor, character memory and emotion systems, voice and animation integration, and SDKs for Unity, Unreal, and web apps. The platform has been used for games, interactive entertainment, branded experiences, and training simulations where conversation practice is valuable. Writers can control tone and limits while still giving players freedom.

item.title: Inworld AI
item.description:
Inworld AI began by giving non-player characters in games personality, memory, and the ability to converse. Developers define a character’s background, goals, and knowledge, and the platform handles dialogue, emotion, and behavior using language models, so players can talk to characters freely instead of choosing from scripted options. Integrations with Unity and Unreal Engine make it easy to add to games.

The company has evolved toward infrastructure for real-time AI applications. Its runtime helps developers build and scale voice and conversational experiences with low latency, and it offers text-to-speech models and tools for combining speech recognition, language models, and voice into agents. Use cases extend from games to training simulations, companions, and consumer apps with talking characters.

item.title: Ludo.ai
item.description:
Ludo.ai aims to speed up the early stages of game development. Designers can brainstorm game concepts and mechanics, get suggestions based on trends in app stores, and generate descriptions and feature lists. A market research tool analyzes top-performing games to show what genres and themes are popular, which helps indie studios and publishers decide what to build.

The platform includes asset generation. It can produce concept art and character designs, sprites and sprite sheets, short animations, UI elements, and sound effects and music from prompts, and convert images into basic 3D models in some plans. Outputs are intended for prototypes and mockups to test ideas quickly, and can be exported for use in engines like Unity.

item.title: Promethean AI
item.description:
Promethean AI addresses the labor involved in building 3D environments. An artist describes what they want in a scene, such as a cluttered study or a forest clearing, and the assistant selects assets from a library, places them with sensible arrangement and variation, and assembles a draft environment. The aim is to automate repetitive dressing and layout so artists can focus on art direction.

The tool learns from the studio’s own assets and preferences, so output stays consistent with the project’s look, and it integrates with common creative software and engines. It was aimed at game studios, film and virtual production teams, and architectural visualization, where large environments must be filled with believable detail.

item.title: Scenario
item.description:
Scenario is built around consistency, which is the main challenge of using generative AI in game production. A studio uploads examples of its art, and Scenario trains a custom model that learns the style, so the characters, props, and environments it generates look like they belong in the same game. Artists can use it to create concepts, variations, and finished assets faster.

The platform covers more than still images. It can generate sprites, textures, icons, and UI elements, create variations of existing pieces, convert images into 3D models, and offers workflows for upscaling and cleaning outputs. An API and plugins connect it to game engines and pipelines, and team features support collaboration and asset management. The focus is on production use by studios and indie developers.

item.title: Convai
item.description:
Convai makes game characters that respond to what players say. A developer defines a character’s personality, backstory, and knowledge, and Convai handles listening to speech, generating replies with a language model, speaking them with a synthetic voice, and driving lip sync and gestures. Plugins integrate with Unity, Unreal Engine, and other platforms.

Characters can also take actions in the game world, such as navigating or interacting with objects, based on conversation. Use cases include immersive games, training simulations, virtual tours, and educational experiences where open-ended dialogue adds value over scripted lines.

item.title: Latitude
item.description:
Latitude makes interactive fiction with AI. Its best-known product, AI Dungeon, lets players describe any action in natural language, and an AI game master responds with the next part of the story. The result is open-ended storytelling that can go in any direction, from fantasy quests to comedy and mystery.

The studio has experimented with other AI-driven games and with platforms for creators who want to build their own AI-powered worlds. It uses a mix of language models, including models it trains and fine-tunes, and offers different tiers of models to subscribers.

item.title: Unakin
item.description:
Unakin targets game studios. Its agents take requests in natural language and help create parts of a game, such as environments, items, interfaces, and gameplay logic, and assist with finding and fixing bugs. The pitch is a smaller team doing more in less time.

Prototyping is a main use, letting designers test ideas before investing heavily. Code assistance for Unity helps developers learn unfamiliar parts of a project.

Independent information is limited, so confirm current availability and pricing on the company’s site. Game development has quality and licensing concerns about AI-generated assets. Alternatives include Unity’s AI tools, Scenario, Inworld, Convai, and general coding assistants like Cursor. Unakin suits game teams exploring AI helpers.
